title: Cosmos DB from C#
description: Use Cosmos DB for NoSQL document storage — create containers, insert and query documents, and handle consistency from C#.

data.text: Azure Cosmos DB is a globally distributed, multi-model NoSQL database. For C# developers, the Azure Cosmos DB SDK for NoSQL (formerly SQL API) provides a natural, LINQ-friendly way to store and query JSON documents with single-digit-millisecond latency at any scale.

data.title: Cosmos DB terms you will use
items: **Account** — the top-level namespace, with a unique endpoint and key
**Database** — a logical container for multiple containers
**Container** — where documents live; equivalent to a SQL table
**Item** — a single JSON document stored in a container
**Partition key** — the property used to distribute items across physical partitions

data.title: Install the Azure.Cosmos package
data.content:
// Package: Azure.Cosmos
dotnet add package Azure.Cosmos

data.title: CosmosSetup.cs — create database and container
PostRepository.cs — insert and upsert a blog post document

data.text: Cosmos DB supports both LINQ (preferred in C#) and raw SQL queries. LINQ is type-safe and integrates with async streams for efficient pagination.

data.title: PostRepository.cs — LINQ and SQL query examples

data.text: Cosmos DB supports optimistic concurrency control via ETags. Include the ETag in the ItemRequestOptions to prevent lost updates when two clients update the same document simultaneously.

data.title: Upsert with ETag — optimistic concurrency control
Choose your partition key carefully
data.text: The partition key cannot be changed after the container is created. Pick a property with high cardinality and even write distribution — for blog posts, blogId is usually a good choice because posts for the same blog are often queried together.

data.title: Build a Cosmos DB-backed post repository
data.description: Create a Cosmos DB container and implement a post repository with insert, upsert, query, and count operations.
steps: Create a Cosmos DB account and BlogDb database in the Azure portal
Define a PostDocument class with Id, BlogId, Title, Content, Tags, PublishedAt
Implement CreatePostAsync, UpsertPostAsync, GetPublishedPostsAsync (LINQ), and CountPostsAsync
Seed three posts and query them — verify the results
data.expectedOutcome: Three posts are stored and retrieved from Cosmos DB; the LINQ query returns only published posts sorted by date.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Cosmos DB stores JSON documents in containers partitioned by a chosen key
Use CreateItemAsync for inserts; UpsertItemAsync when the document may already exist
Query with LINQ via GetItemLinqQueryable or raw SQL via GetItemQueryIterator
Use ETags with ReplaceItemAsync for optimistic concurrency control
data.takeaway: Cosmos DB provides globally distributed NoSQL with a C# SDK that feels native — LINQ queries, async streams, and strong typing make it a natural fit for ASP.NET Core document workloads.
